1	# Repository Parallelizer
     2	
     3	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
     4	
     5	## What Is This?
     6	
     7	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
     8	
     9	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    10	
    11	## Features
    12	
    13	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    14	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    15	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    16	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    17	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup. The project dashboard supports real-time filtering by name/ID/description, repository filtering, and sort by alphabetical or last-activity order.
    18	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    19	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files).
    20	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    21	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    22	
    23	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    24	
    25	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    26	
    27	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    30	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    31	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    32	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    33	
    34	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    35	
    36	## Requirements
    37	
    38	- **Node.js** >= 18
    39	- **npm** >= 9
    40	- **git** >= 2.28
    41	
    42	## Quick Start
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# Clone and build
    46	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    47	cd repo-parallelizer
    48	npm install
    49	npm run build
    50	
    51	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    52	npm link
    53	paralizer setup
    54	
    55	# Launch the GUI
    56	paralizer serve
    57	```
    58	
    59	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    60	
    61	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    62	
    63	```bash
    64	# Unix / macOS
    65	./menu.sh
    66	
    67	# Windows
    68	menu.cmd
    69	```
    70	
    71	### CLI commands
    72	
    73	| Command | Description |
    74	|---------|-------------|
    75	| `paralizer` | Open the interactive CLI menu |
    76	| `paralizer serve` | Start the GUI server directly |
    77	| `paralizer setup` | Run the setup wizard |
    78	| `paralizer docs` | Generate project documentation |
    79	
    80	## Start with Windows
    81	
    82	1. Press `Win + R`, type the following command to open your user Startup folder, and press **Enter**:
    83	   ```
    84	   shell:startup
    85	   ```
    86	   *(This opens the folder: `C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`)*
    87	
    88	2. In that folder, right-click an empty area and select **New** > **Text Document**.
    89	3. Name it `start-repo-parallelizer.vbs` (ensure you delete the `.txt` extension!).
    90	4. Right-click the new file, select **Edit** (or open it with Notepad/VS Code), and paste the following code into it:
    91	
    92	   ```vbscript
    93	   Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
    94	   ' 0 means the window will be hidden, so you don't have a lingering terminal
    95	   WshShell.Run "cmd /c paralizer serve", 0
    96	   Set WshShell = Nothing
    97	   ```
    98	
    99	   > **Requires `npm link`** — run `npm link` once in the project folder so `paralizer` is available globally.

1	# Constraints & Conventions
     2	
     3	## TypeScript Import Extensions
     4	
     5	All relative imports **must** include the `.js` extension:
     6	
     7	```typescript
     8	// Correct
     9	import { MyClass } from './my-module.js';
    10	
    11	// Wrong — compile error + runtime failure
    12	import { MyClass } from './my-module';
    13	```
    14	
    15	This is a strict requirement of the `Node16` module resolution setting. TypeScript maps `.js` → `.ts` at compile time and emits `.js` unchanged for Node.js at runtime.
    16	
    17	## Git Subprocess Security
    18	
    19	- All Git commands use `shell: false` — no shell expansion, globbing, or metacharacter processing.
    20	- Arguments are passed as a typed `string[]` directly to `spawn()`.
    21	- Error messages use only `args[0]` (the subcommand name), never the full args array, to avoid leaking credential-bearing URLs.
    22	- `RepositoryManager.add()` redacts embedded credentials from URLs before interpolating into error messages.
    23	- `runGit()` always sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=echo` on every spawned subprocess. This prevents interactive credential prompts and credential-helper (osxkeychain, libsecret) blocking on unauthenticated requests. Do not remove either env var.
    24	- **Standing rule — credential stripping in git error output:** When credential injection is wired into future WPs (i.e., `injectCredentials()` is used to append tokens to URLs before passing to `runGit()`/`runGitOrThrow()`), all code paths that surface `GitResult.stderr` in thrown Error messages, log output, or API responses **must** apply `stripEmbeddedCredentials()` (from `src/git/git-credentials.ts`) to the stderr string first. Git may echo the credentialed URL back in error messages (e.g., `fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/... not found`), which would expose the PAT. This is a non-optional security control for every credential-injection WP.
    25	- **Credential injection lifetime contract:** `injectCredentials()` must only be called immediately before a git subprocess invocation — never stored or returned through API boundaries. The injected URL must not appear in log output, API responses, or Error messages without first passing through `stripEmbeddedCredentials()`.
    26	- **Pre-embedded-credentials passthrough:** If a repo URL already contains embedded credentials (detected via `hasEmbeddedCredentials()`) and the URL’s host is not present in the `gitCredentials` map, `injectCredentials()` returns the URL unchanged — including its pre-existing credentials. Orchestrator implementations **must** call `hasEmbeddedCredentials()` before `injectCredentials()` and decide explicitly whether to strip and re-inject or reject the URL.- **Token masking rule (API responses):** The `gitCredentials` field in `AppConfig` / `config.json` stores **plaintext** tokens. No API handler, logger, or error message may expose a plaintext token in any response. All credential API responses must pass the map through `buildMaskedCredentials()` (in `src/server/routes/config.ts`) before serialisation — this applies `maskToken()` to every value, producing `****` + last-4-chars (e.g. `****abc1`). Tokens shorter than 4 characters are fully masked as `****`. This is a non-optional security control: any new credential endpoint **must** apply `buildMaskedCredentials()` before calling `sendJson()`.
    27	## Stateless Managers
    28	
    29	All model managers (`RepositoryManager`, `ProjectManager`, `WorkspaceManager`) re-read their backing JSON file from disk on **every** public method call. There is no in-memory cache. This ensures concurrent writes from other processes are always reflected.
    30	
    31	## ID Validation Rules
    32	
    33	| Entity | Format | Validation Function |
    34	|---|---|---|
    35	| Repository ID | Lowercase kebab-case (`a-z0-9`, segments separated by `-`) | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    36	| Project ID | Lowercase kebab-case | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    37	| Workspace ID | 2–10 uppercase ASCII letters (`A-Z`) | `isValidWorkspaceId()` |
    38	
    39	Path-traversal sequences, uppercase characters (for kebab-case IDs), spaces, and other invalid formats are rejected with a descriptive error.
    40	
    41	## The STABLE Workspace Invariant
    42	
    43	Every project has exactly one workspace with ID `"STABLE"`. It is auto-created when a project is created and **cannot be removed or renamed**. The STABLE workspace is intended for the remote's default branch.
    44	
    45	## Path Resolution
    46	
    47	Both `storageFolder` and `projectsFolder` in `config.json` accept relative or absolute paths:
    48	
    49	- **Relative paths** are resolved against the tool root (directory containing `package.json`), regardless of the current working directory when the tool is invoked.
    50	- **Absolute paths** are used as-is.
    51	
    52	## Configuration
    53	
    54	- `config.json` is created by copying `config.dist.json`. It is not committed (gitignored).
    55	- The `_instructions` key in `config.dist.json` is an editorial note and is not a valid config field. Remove it from `config.json`.
    56	- `initializeStorage()` is idempotent — re-running it does not overwrite existing files.
    57	- **`DEFAULTS` Pick maintenance:** The exported `DEFAULTS` constant in `src/config/config.ts` is typed as `Pick<AppConfig, 'cloneDepth' | 'serverPort' | 'gitPollingIntervalSeconds' | 'notesCardHeight' | 'notesColumns'>`. When a new non-optional, non-required `AppConfig` field with a sensible default is added, **three** coordinated changes are required: (1) add the field key to the `Pick` union, (2) add the field's default value to the `DEFAULTS` object literal, and (3) add the fallback guard in `loadConfig()` (e.g. `typeof raw['field'] === 'number' ? raw['field'] : DEFAULTS.field`). Omitting step (1) is a TypeScript compile error; omitting steps (2)–(3) causes the field to be `undefined` at runtime for configs that predate the new field.
    58	
    59	## Test Conventions
    60	
    61	- **Test runner:** Node.js built-in test runner (`node --test`).
    62	- **Cleanup:** All tests creating temporary files must register a `process.on('exit')` handler for synchronous cleanup, in addition to `afterAll`. The `'exit'` event fires on `SIGINT` or crash.
    63	- **Network tests:** Tests requiring outbound internet set `SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1` to self-skip.
    64	- **Fake-git binary pattern:** To test CLI argument construction (e.g., verifying credential-injected URLs are passed correctly to `cloneRepository()`), use a fake git binary stub rather than module mocking or network calls. The stub is a shell script placed in a uniquely-prefixed temp directory that is prepended to `process.env.PATH` for the test duration; it writes all received arguments to a capture file and exits with a non-zero code. The original PATH is always restored in a `finally` block. This approach is necessary because modern git (2.x/libcurl) strips embedded credentials from its own error messages, making the injected-URL string unavailable in `stderr`. The shared implementation lives in `src/tests/test-helpers.ts` (`setupFakeGit()`). **Note:** PATH mutation is not concurrency-safe — this pattern is safe only because the test runner executes test files sequentially.
    65	
    66	## GUI Frontend Conventions
    67	
    68	- **Router injection:** Views needing programmatic navigation export `setRouter(router)` and receive the router via dependency injection from `app.js`. Direct imports of `router.js` from views are forbidden (circular dependency).
    69	- **Cleanup contract:** Views with side-effects (intervals, event listeners) must return a cleanup function from their render entry point. The router calls it before rendering the next view.
    70	- **No framework:** Vanilla JavaScript with ES modules. No build step for the frontend.
    71	- **JSON key normalisation:** The backend uses PascalCase keys (`Id`, `Name`, `Url`). The `normalise.js` utility maps them to camelCase for frontend use.
    72	
    73	## Vendor CSS Assets
    74	
    75	The `gui/public/css/vendor/` directory contains CSS files copied from `node_modules` by the `copy-vendor` npm script. These are **generated artifacts** and must not be committed to version control (gitignored). After cloning the repo, run `npm install` — the `postinstall` hook will automatically populate the vendor directory. Currently contains `pico.classless.min.css` from `@picocss/pico`.
    76	
    77	## Build Output
    78	
    79	- Compiled output goes to `dist/`. Source maps are generated alongside each `.js` file.
    80	- `dist/` is excluded from version control.
    81	- `dist/index.js` does not carry the executable bit after `tsc`. Use `npm link` or `node dist/index.js`.
    82	
    83	## Request Body Limit
    84	
    85	`parseJsonBody()` enforces a **1 MB** request body size limit.
    86	
    87	## Timeout Constants
    88	
    89	| Constant | Value | Used By |
    90	|---|---|---|
    91	| `CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS` | 120,000 ms (2 min) | `cloneRepository()` via orchestrators |
    92	| `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | 30,000 ms (30 sec) | `fetchRemote()` via polling and branch operations |
    93	
    94	## Config Validation Constants
    95	
    96	All validation bounds for `AppConfig` fields are defined in `src/config/config.constants.ts` and imported by route handlers. Route-level validation enforces integer-only values within these ranges; `loadConfig()` applies defaults but does not clamp out-of-range values.
    97	
    98	| Constant | Value | Field | Description |
    99	|---|---|---|---|

1	# Constraints & Conventions
     2	
     3	## TypeScript Import Extensions
     4	
     5	All relative imports **must** include the `.js` extension:
     6	
     7	```typescript
     8	// Correct
     9	import { MyClass } from './my-module.js';
    10	
    11	// Wrong — compile error + runtime failure
    12	import { MyClass } from './my-module';
    13	```
    14	
    15	This is a strict requirement of the `Node16` module resolution setting. TypeScript maps `.js` → `.ts` at compile time and emits `.js` unchanged for Node.js at runtime.
    16	
    17	## Git Subprocess Security
    18	
    19	- All Git commands use `shell: false` — no shell expansion, globbing, or metacharacter processing.
    20	- Arguments are passed as a typed `string[]` directly to `spawn()`.
    21	- Error messages use only `args[0]` (the subcommand name), never the full args array, to avoid leaking credential-bearing URLs.
    22	- `RepositoryManager.add()` redacts embedded credentials from URLs before interpolating into error messages.
    23	- `runGit()` always sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=echo` on every spawned subprocess. This prevents interactive credential prompts and credential-helper (osxkeychain, libsecret) blocking on unauthenticated requests. Do not remove either env var.
    24	- **Standing rule — credential stripping in git error output:** When credential injection is wired into future WPs (i.e., `injectCredentials()` is used to append tokens to URLs before passing to `runGit()`/`runGitOrThrow()`), all code paths that surface `GitResult.stderr` in thrown Error messages, log output, or API responses **must** apply `stripEmbeddedCredentials()` (from `src/git/git-credentials.ts`) to the stderr string first. Git may echo the credentialed URL back in error messages (e.g., `fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/... not found`), which would expose the PAT. This is a non-optional security control for every credential-injection WP.
    25	- **Credential injection lifetime contract:** `injectCredentials()` must only be called immediately before a git subprocess invocation — never stored or returned through API boundaries. The injected URL must not appear in log output, API responses, or Error messages without first passing through `stripEmbeddedCredentials()`.
    26	- **Pre-embedded-credentials passthrough:** If a repo URL already contains embedded credentials (detected via `hasEmbeddedCredentials()`) and the URL’s host is not present in the `gitCredentials` map, `injectCredentials()` returns the URL unchanged — including its pre-existing credentials. Orchestrator implementations **must** call `hasEmbeddedCredentials()` before `injectCredentials()` and decide explicitly whether to strip and re-inject or reject the URL.- **Token masking rule (API responses):** The `gitCredentials` field in `AppConfig` / `config.json` stores **plaintext** tokens. No API handler, logger, or error message may expose a plaintext token in any response. All credential API responses must pass the array through `buildMaskedCredentials()` (in `src/server/routes/config.ts`) before serialisation — this applies `maskToken()` to every `token` field in each `GitCredentialEntry`, producing `****` + last-4-chars (e.g. `****abc1`). Tokens shorter than 4 characters are fully masked as `****`. This is a non-optional security control: any new credential endpoint **must** apply `buildMaskedCredentials()` before calling `sendJson()`.
    27	## Stateless Managers
    28	
    29	All model managers (`RepositoryManager`, `ProjectManager`, `WorkspaceManager`) re-read their backing JSON file from disk on **every** public method call. There is no in-memory cache. This ensures concurrent writes from other processes are always reflected.
    30	
    31	## ID Validation Rules
    32	
    33	| Entity | Format | Validation Function |
    34	|---|---|---|
    35	| Repository ID | Lowercase kebab-case (`a-z0-9`, segments separated by `-`) | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    36	| Project ID | Lowercase kebab-case | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    37	| Workspace ID | 2–10 uppercase ASCII letters (`A-Z`) | `isValidWorkspaceId()` |
    38	
    39	Path-traversal sequences, uppercase characters (for kebab-case IDs), spaces, and other invalid formats are rejected with a descriptive error.
    40	
    41	## The STABLE Workspace Invariant
    42	
    43	Every project has exactly one workspace with ID `"STABLE"`. It is auto-created when a project is created and **cannot be removed or renamed**. The STABLE workspace is intended for the remote's default branch.
    44	
    45	## Path Resolution
    46	
    47	Both `storageFolder` and `projectsFolder` in `config.json` accept relative or absolute paths:
    48	
    49	- **Relative paths** are resolved against the tool root (directory containing `package.json`), regardless of the current working directory when the tool is invoked.
    50	- **Absolute paths** are used as-is.
    51	
    52	## Configuration
    53	
    54	- `config.json` is created by copying `config.dist.json`. It is not committed (gitignored).
    55	- The `_instructions` key in `config.dist.json` is an editorial note and is not a valid config field. Remove it from `config.json`.
    56	- `initializeStorage()` is idempotent — re-running it does not overwrite existing files.
    57	- **`DEFAULTS` Pick maintenance:** The exported `DEFAULTS` constant in `src/config/config.ts` is typed as `Pick<AppConfig, 'cloneDepth' | 'serverPort' | 'gitPollingIntervalSeconds' | 'notesCardHeight' | 'notesColumns'>`. When a new non-optional, non-required `AppConfig` field with a sensible default is added, **three** coordinated changes are required: (1) add the field key to the `Pick` union, (2) add the field's default value to the `DEFAULTS` object literal, and (3) add the fallback guard in `loadConfig()` (e.g. `typeof raw['field'] === 'number' ? raw['field'] : DEFAULTS.field`). Omitting step (1) is a TypeScript compile error; omitting steps (2)–(3) causes the field to be `undefined` at runtime for configs that predate the new field.
    58	
    59	## Schema Version Policy
    60	
    61	The `SchemaVersion` field on `BaseStore` tracks structural changes to persisted JSON store files. The rule is defined in `src/storage/storage.types.ts`:
    62	
    63	- **Do NOT bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** when adding an **optional** field. Existing JSON files that lack the field are still valid — no migration is required.
    64	- **Do bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** (and add a migration step) for breaking changes: removing a required field, renaming a field, or changing the type of an existing field in a way that would cause older JSON files to fail validation or produce incorrect behaviour.
    65	
    66	**Example:** `Repository.CredentialId` is an optional field addition — existing `repositories.json` files remain valid without it. No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump was needed for this change.
    67	
    68	## Test Conventions
    69	
    70	- **Test runner:** Node.js built-in test runner (`node --test`).
    71	- **Cleanup:** All tests creating temporary files must register a `process.on('exit')` handler for synchronous cleanup, in addition to `afterAll`. The `'exit'` event fires on `SIGINT` or crash.
    72	- **Network tests:** Tests requiring outbound internet set `SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1` to self-skip.
    73	- **Fake-git binary pattern:** To test CLI argument construction (e.g., verifying credential-injected URLs are passed correctly to `cloneRepository()`), use a fake git binary stub rather than module mocking or network calls. The stub is a shell script placed in a uniquely-prefixed temp directory that is prepended to `process.env.PATH` for the test duration; it writes all received arguments to a capture file and exits with a non-zero code. The original PATH is always restored in a `finally` block. This approach is necessary because modern git (2.x/libcurl) strips embedded credentials from its own error messages, making the injected-URL string unavailable in `stderr`. The shared implementation lives in `src/tests/test-helpers.ts` (`setupFakeGit()`). **Note:** PATH mutation is not concurrency-safe — this pattern is safe only because the test runner executes test files sequentially.
    74	
    75	## GUI Frontend Conventions
    76	
    77	- **Router injection:** Views needing programmatic navigation export `setRouter(router)` and receive the router via dependency injection from `app.js`. Direct imports of `router.js` from views are forbidden (circular dependency).
    78	- **Cleanup contract:** Views with side-effects (intervals, event listeners) must return a cleanup function from their render entry point. The router calls it before rendering the next view.
    79	- **No framework:** Vanilla JavaScript with ES modules. No build step for the frontend.
    80	- **JSON key normalisation:** The backend uses PascalCase keys (`Id`, `Name`, `Url`). The `normalise.js` utility maps them to camelCase for frontend use.
    81	
    82	## Vendor CSS Assets
    83	
    84	The `gui/public/css/vendor/` directory contains CSS files copied from `node_modules` by the `copy-vendor` npm script. These are **generated artifacts** and must not be committed to version control (gitignored). After cloning the repo, run `npm install` — the `postinstall` hook will automatically populate the vendor directory. Currently contains `pico.classless.min.css` from `@picocss/pico`.
    85	
    86	## Build Output
    87	
    88	- Compiled output goes to `dist/`. Source maps are generated alongside each `.js` file.
    89	- `dist/` is excluded from version control.
    90	- `dist/index.js` does not carry the executable bit after `tsc`. Use `npm link` or `node dist/index.js`.
    91	
    92	## Request Body Limit
    93	
    94	`parseJsonBody()` enforces a **1 MB** request body size limit.

    97	
    98	| Constant | Value | Used By |
